text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — tokenizer_cpu_spike on prod-cluster-eu-west-2. Multiple pods OOMKilled and restarted. Pager: @alex-m (primary). Severity: P1.

oncall-bot: symptoms: rapid CPU usage on tokenizer containers, linear increase in request latency, 5xx spike for text-gen route. Affected service: serving-runtime/tokenizer.

alex-m: reading it now. seeing alerts in grafana: cpu > 95% on node pool 'inference-cpu-2' and several pods in CrashLoopBackOff. Paging priya.

priya_s: on it. any customer-facing alerts yet?

lina-cs: support reported a small cohort of customer apps in EU hitting 503s since 09:02 UTC, about 120 requests/min failing. Customers: two mid-market tenants (acct ids redacted). ETA for full impact assessment in 10m.

alex-m: ok mitigation plan: 1) reduce tokenizer concurrency on serving runtime via feature flag 2) scale out CPU pool temporarily 3) cordon problematic node(s) 4) add temporary prefix caching. Initiating step 1 now.

jamie_r: context from runtime: we've seen a tokenizer hotloop when inputs contain lots of long unicode whitespace + repeated non-breaking spaces; recent client change may be increasing average tokenization cost. Also a small regression in tokenizer cache eviction from last deploy that reduced cache effectiveness under burst.

nikhil_i: scaling node pool now: +4 nodes (m5a-large equiv), request sent to autoscaler. I'll also preemptively drain node ip-10-2-43-17 which shows repeated pod OOM.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaling group inference-cpu-2 desiredCapacity 6 -> 10. Expected nodes provisioning 1801203510 - 1801203600.

alex-m: toggled runtime flag tokenizer.max_concurrency=2 for route /v1/generate (was 8). This will shed some throughput but protects CPU.

priya_s: running a quick grep on recent logs for the hot input pattern. found ~300 requests with long whitespace sequences from 09:01:30 - 09:03:10. Example payload (sanitized):
```
{
  "input": "Hello\u00A0\u00A0\u00A0...<repeated>..."
}
```

rory-ml: crossing this with client telemetry: looks like one of the PLG sample apps started sending pasted docs with non-breaking spaces; heuristic failure. Could be benign but volume is high.

lina-cs: update: customers A and B hit ~30% errors each, some timed out at 30s. We're notifying them for mitigation (advise smaller chunks). Creating incident status page note.

alex-m: cordoned ip-10-2-43-17 and evicted tokenizers on that node, they're rescheduling. Still seeing elevated CPU on other nodes, so scaling might help.

jamie_r: I'm pushing a hotfix to tokenizer that adds a cheap pre-scan to collapse long runs of NBSP/whitespace before tokenization. Patch is tiny but needs canary. preparing image: ghcr.io/redwood/tokenizer:v2.3-hotfix.

priya_s: while jamie's canary builds we should enable local prefix/KV cache bypass to avoid evict churn. Alex, can we enable cache bypass for long prefix paths?

alex-m: yes flipping runtime config to bypass_kv_on_long_prefix=true for now. Doing canary rollout 10% to eu-west region only.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated for image ghcr.io/redwood/tokenizer:v2.3-hotfix to service serving-runtime-tokenizer (10%).

jamie_r: canary pods up at 1801203580. Observing their CPU: baseline 12% vs 92% on old pods when feeding problematic payload. This looks promising.

priya_s: good sign. I'm watching overall 5xx rate — started to drop around 1801203605. Lina, confirm support ticket updates?

lina-cs: support: notified customers A/B with recommended short-term workarounds. They've acknowledged and will retry with smaller payloads. I'll keep them updated.

nikhil_i: nodes from autoscaler are Ready. Draining/eviction finished for the bad node. We should see headroom in ~2m.

alex-m: given canary numbers and reduced 5xx, I'm going to roll the fix to 50% then 100% if stable. Also keeping tokenizer.max_concurrency=2 until end of incident.

jamie_r: rolling to 50% now.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout to 50% at 1801203660.

priya_s: monitoring heap/CPU and OOM events. No new OOMs since 1801203635. Good. Still watch for node flaps.

rory-ml: adding small automated guard in runtime to reject inputs with > 10k consecutive NBSP-like chars with 400 instead of letting tokenizer spin. I'll open PR now; we can merge and hot-deploy later if needed.

alex-m: please do. For now we have mitigations: scale, canary, concurrency limit, cache bypass. Lifting severity from P1 to P2 at 1801203690.

lina-cs: customers on the thread confirmed partial recovery. I'll send the postmortem to the affected account owners once we have root cause.

priya_s: note for postmortem: contributing factors: 1) high-volume malformed inputs with long NBSP runs 2) recent cache eviction regression 3) tokenizer does expensive preproc per request 4) autoscaler capacity lag. Action items: add input-size guards, revert/repair cache eviction logic, improve autoscaler headroom, add synthetic test with long NBSP runs.

jamie_r: created hotfix PR and follow-ups: tokenizer pre-scan merged to main, backported to release branch. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/tokenizer/pulls/4321

nikhil_i: follow-ups for infra: reduce autoscaler scale-up time (action ticket INFRA-908), add node taint for OOM-prone pods (INFRA-909).

alex-m: thanks all. I'll prepare incident summary and schedule a follow-up retro tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Marking incident as transitioning to recovery.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> P2 at 1801203690. Resolved: tokenizer OOMs mitigated, customer impact reduced.

lina-cs: filing customer incident emails now.

priya_s: last check: no new OOMs in 7m, 5xx rate back to baseline. closing channel in 30m unless regressions.

alex-m: closing notes: keep the concurrency cap until we verify autoscaler config and merge the NBSP guard in prod. Assigning follow-ups to owners in the PM notes. Great work. :thumbsup:
